title: No pan or unsuitable cookware
shortDescription: Cooking zone does not detect a magnetic pan.
fullDescription:
Samsung induction cooktops display E1 when a zone is turned on but no ferrous pan is on the surface, or the pan is too small or not magnetic.

The cooktop pauses heating after about 60 seconds and shows the code until a compatible pan is placed.

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Place a fridge magnet on the pan base. If it does not stick firmly, the pan is not induction compatible.

fixSteps.title: Check size
fixSteps.instruction: Use a pan that covers at least 70 percent of the cooking zone marked on the glass.

fixSteps.title: Center the pan
fixSteps.instruction: Place the pan in the middle of the engraved circle.

whenToCallPro: No service needed unless E1 also shows with a known induction pan.

faq.q: How do I know my pan is induction compatible?
faq.a: If a magnet sticks firmly to the bottom, the pan will work.

title: Zone overheated
shortDescription: Cooking zone temperature exceeded the safe limit.
fullDescription:
E2 means the IGBT or coil temperature sensor measured a value above the protection threshold. Empty pans, warped bottoms, or a blocked cooling fan are the typical causes.

The cooktop locks the zone until temperature drops back to a safe range.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pans and let the surface cool for 20 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm nothing blocks the cabinet vents below the cooktop.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: If E2 returns at low heat, a technician should check the cooling fan and IGBT thermistor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if E2 returns after the unit cools and vents are clear.

faq.q: Can I keep cooking on other zones?
faq.a: Yes, only the affected zone locks out.

title: Mains voltage too low
shortDescription: Supply voltage is below the operating range.
fullDescription:
Samsung induction cooktops require a stable 208-240 V supply. E3 indicates the input dropped below roughly 180 V.

Utility brownouts, loose breaker connections, or shared circuits with high-draw appliances often trigger this.

fixSteps.title: Check breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Open the panel and confirm both legs of the 240 V breaker are seated and not warm.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: With the cooktop off, measure between L1 and L2 at the terminal block. Expect 220-244 V.

fixSteps.title: Call electrician
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is below 200 V, call an electrician to inspect the panel and supply.

whenToCallPro: Always call a licensed electrician for panel work.

faq.a: Only a true sine inverter rated above the cooktop's nameplate amps.

title: Mains voltage too high
fullDescription:
E4 protects the IGBT module from over-voltage. Common causes are a lost neutral on the service, an aggressive surge, or a misconfigured 277 V circuit.

The cooktop locks until voltage returns to the normal window.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Switch the breaker off for 5 minutes, then back on.

fixSteps.title: Verify supply
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician verify L-N is 120 V on each leg and L-L is 240 V.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is correct and E4 persists, the power board needs replacement.

whenToCallPro: Open neutrals are dangerous. Call an electrician immediately.

faq.a: Yes, kill the breaker until the supply is verified safe.

title: IGBT temperature sensor fault
shortDescription: The IGBT thermistor reports an out-of-range value.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates the temperature sensor on the inverter IGBT is open or shorted. It can be caused by a disconnected sensor lead, a failed thermistor, or a damaged power board.

The affected zone is disabled until the sensor reads correctly.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker power before any access.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: From below, find the thermistor on the IGBT heatsink and reseat its connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: If the resistance is far from spec at room temperature, replace the sensor.

whenToCallPro: Most homeowners should let a technician access the inverter.

faq.q: Is the cooktop safe to use?
faq.a: Yes on other zones, but the affected zone is locked.

title: Cooling fan fault
shortDescription: The internal cooling fan is not running at speed.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates the fan tachometer signal is missing or out of range. Dust, a loose connector, or a failed fan motor are typical causes.

The cooktop reduces power or stops to protect the inverter.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum vents
fixSteps.instruction: From below, vacuum dust from intake and exhaust grilles.

fixSteps.title: Reseat plug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and reconnect the fan plug at the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If the fan does not spin freely or hums, replace it.

whenToCallPro: Call if you are not comfortable removing the cooktop from the cabinet.

faq.q: Why is the fan dusty so fast?
faq.a: Open kitchens vacuum airborne grease and lint into the chassis.

title: Touch communication error
shortDescription: Lost data link between touch panel and main board.
fullDescription:
E8 means the user-interface board cannot reach the main control. A loose ribbon cable, moisture in the connector, or a failed board causes the fault.

No zone responds until communication is restored.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker power for 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Carefully unclip and reseat the ribbon between the UI and main board.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI board
fixSteps.instruction: If the cable is good, the UI board likely needs replacement.

whenToCallPro: Most owners should let a tech open the chassis.

faq.a: Samsung does not field-update induction firmware on these models.

title: Touch key stuck
shortDescription: A control key reads as held continuously.
fullDescription:
E9 appears when the touch surface detects pressure on a key for more than ten seconds at startup. Spilled liquid, a wet cloth, or pressed objects on the controls are the usual cause.

The cooktop disables itself until the surface is clean and clear.

fixSteps.title: Wipe dry
fixSteps.instruction: Dry the entire glass with a clean towel and remove anything resting on it.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut the breaker for 5 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Replace glass
fixSteps.instruction: If the glass is cracked under the touch zone, replace the glass-touch assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call only if the glass shows damage.

faq.q: Why does this trip during cleaning?
faq.a: Pressing keys with a wet sponge mimics a finger.

title: Coil drive frequency fault
shortDescription: Inverter cannot reach the target switching frequency.
fullDescription:
C-F2 indicates the inverter detected an out-of-range coil drive frequency, often caused by an unsuitable pan, a cracked coil, or a failing IGBT.

The zone shuts down to prevent component damage.

causes.cause: Pan with thin or distorted base

fixSteps.title: Try a different pan
fixSteps.instruction: Test the zone with a known good cast iron skillet.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil
fixSteps.instruction: From below, check the coil ferrites for cracks or burn marks.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil or IGBT
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the coil assembly or inverter, depending on findings.

whenToCallPro: Coil and IGBT work is best left to a technician.

faq.q: Can a thin steel pan trigger this?
faq.a: Yes, the inverter cannot lock onto a poorly-coupled pan.

title: Child lock cannot be cleared
shortDescription: Cooktop refuses to exit child lock mode.
fullDescription:
Er03 appears when the cooktop sees stuck residual signals on the lock key, or the EEPROM stored a bad lock state.

A full power cycle plus the lock key combo usually clears the code.

fixSteps.title: Dry surface
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe and dry the entire glass.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Hold lock
fixSteps.instruction: After power returns, hold the lock key for 5 seconds.

whenToCallPro: Only if the code returns after a clean power cycle.

faq.q: How do I prevent kids from triggering this?
faq.a: Use the lock symbol intentionally; do not let kids press random keys with wet hands.
